at observere.explanation: "At observere" means "to observe", to watch something closely in order to learn from it. It is used for science, nature and police work: at observere fuglene (to observe the birds).

sentence.da: Lægen vil **observere** patienten natten over.
sentence.en: The doctor wants to observe the patient overnight.

at offentliggøre.explanation: "At offentliggøre" means "to publish / make public", to let everyone know something that was private. It is used for results, lists and decisions: Regeringen offentliggør planen (The government makes the plan public).

sentence.da: Avisen vil **offentliggøre** resultaterne på mandag.
sentence.en: The newspaper will publish the results on Monday.

at ofre.explanation: "At ofre" means "to sacrifice", to give up something valuable for a person or a goal. It can be time or money: Hun ofrer sin weekend (She gives up her weekend). It is also used for an offering to a god: at ofre til guderne (to make an offering to the gods).

sentence.da: Mange forældre vil **ofre** alt for deres børn.
sentence.en: Many parents will sacrifice everything for their children.

at omdanne.explanation: "At omdanne" means "to transform", to change something completely into a new form or use. Om (over) at the start carries the idea of making it over into something different. It fits people and ideas too: Oplevelsen omdannede ham (The experience transformed him).

sentence.da: De vil **omdanne** den gamle fabrik til billige lejligheder.
sentence.en: They want to turn the old factory into cheap apartments.

at omfatte.explanation: "At omfatte" means "to include", used when a whole is made up of certain parts or covers a range. The whole is the one that does it, not a person: Kurset omfatter fem emner (The course covers five topics).

sentence.da: Billetten kan **omfatte** både mad og drikke.
sentence.en: The ticket can include both food and drinks.

at omformulere.explanation: "At omformulere" means "to rephrase", to say or write the same thing again in other words. You do it when your first version was unclear or did not suit the situation. Om (over, again) gives the idea of a new version of the same message.

sentence.da: Hvis folk ikke forstår dig, må du **omformulere** spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: If people do not understand you, you have to rephrase the question.

at omgive.explanation: "At omgive" means "to surround": to be on all sides of something: En mur omgiver byen (A wall surrounds the town). You often see it as omgivet af (surrounded by): Huset er omgivet af skov (The house is surrounded by forest).

sentence.da: Man kan **omgive** en have med en grøn hæk.
sentence.en: You can surround a garden with a green hedge.

at omgå.explanation: "At omgå" means "to bypass" or "to get around" a problem, a rule or an obstacle, often by finding a clever way past: omgå et problem (get around a problem). Do not confuse it with at omgås (to socialize), which only adds an s.

sentence.da: Lastbilen må **omgå** byen, fordi broen er lukket.
sentence.en: The truck has to go around the town because the bridge is closed.

at omgås.explanation: "At omgås" means "to associate with" or "to socialize": to spend time with people regularly: Jeg omgås mest folk fra arbejdet (I mostly spend time with people from work). Do not confuse it with at omgå (to bypass), which has no s.

sentence.da: Det er rart at **omgås** mennesker, som man har det godt med.
sentence.en: It is nice to socialize with people you feel good with.

at omringe.explanation: "At omringe" means "to surround", to stand on all sides of someone or something so that there is no way past. It is used for crowds and soldiers, but also for things: En mur omringer haven (A wall surrounds the garden).

sentence.da: Politiet vil **omringe** huset, så ingen kan flygte.
sentence.en: The police want to surround the house so nobody can flee.

at omstille sig.explanation: "At omstille sig" means "to adapt", to change how you work or live so that it fits a new situation, such as new rules or a new job. Sig means "yourself" and changes with the person: jeg omstiller mig (I adapt), du omstiller dig (you adapt), de omstiller sig (they adapt).

sentence.da: Firmaet må **omstille sig**, når kunderne vil købe på nettet.
sentence.en: The company has to adapt when customers want to buy online.

at omstrukturere.explanation: "At omstrukturere" means "to restructure": to arrange a company, a school or a system in a new way: Kommunen omstrukturerer sine skoler (The city is restructuring its schools). The om at the start works like "re-" in other words, such as at omskrive (to rewrite).

sentence.da: Firmaet er nødt til at **omstrukturere**, fordi salget falder.
sentence.en: The company has to restructure because sales are falling.

at omtale.explanation: "At omtale" means "to mention" or "to refer to", to speak of a person or thing, often in a newspaper or in public. With som it says how someone is seen: Hun omtales som byens bedste kok (She is referred to as the best cook in town).

sentence.da: Aviserne kan **omtale** en ny film, før den kommer i biografen.
sentence.en: The newspapers can mention a new film before it comes to the cinema.

at opbevare.explanation: "At opbevare" means "to store", to keep something in a place until it is needed or so that it stays safe. It fits food, documents, tools and medicine: Mælk skal opbevares i køleskabet (Milk must be kept in the fridge).

sentence.da: Du kan **opbevare** cyklen i kælderen om vinteren.
sentence.en: You can store the bike in the basement in winter.

at opbygge.explanation: "At opbygge" means "to build up", to create something that grows slowly step by step: a business, muscles or trust. For a house, use at bygge (to build) instead.

sentence.da: Man kan ikke **opbygge** stærke muskler på én uge.
sentence.en: You cannot build up strong muscles in one week.

at opdage.explanation: "At opdage" means "to discover", finding or noticing something you did not know about: Jeg opdagede en fejl (I noticed a mistake). It often comes as a surprise: Hun opdagede, at tasken var væk (She discovered that the bag was gone).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **opdage** nye steder på rejsen.
sentence.en: We would like to discover new places on the trip.

at opdatere.explanation: "At opdatere" means "to update", to make something new or current, like a program or a list: Hun opdaterer listen hver uge (She updates the list every week).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **opdatere** min telefon i aften.
sentence.en: I want to update my phone tonight.

at opdele.explanation: "At opdele" means "to divide", to split something into several parts or groups: Læreren opdeler klassen i fire hold (The teacher splits the class into four teams). At dele (to share) can also mean that, but it is more about giving a part to someone else.

sentence.da: Vi kan **opdele** kagen i otte lige store stykker.
sentence.en: We can divide the cake into eight equal pieces.

at opdrage.explanation: "At opdrage" means "to raise (a child)", to teach a child how to behave and what matters in life. It is about manners and values over many years, not only about feeding and caring for the child.

sentence.da: Forældre skal **opdrage** deres børn til at sige tak og undskyld.
sentence.en: Parents must raise their children to say thank you and sorry.

at operere.explanation: "At operere" means "to operate", on a patient: Lægen opererer i morgen (The doctor operates tomorrow). It is also used for a business working somewhere: Firmaet opererer i Europa (The company operates in Europe).

sentence.da: Lægen skal **operere** min mor i morgen.
sentence.en: The doctor is going to operate on my mother tomorrow.

at opfange.explanation: "At opfange" means "to pick up" or "to catch" something that is sent or passing by, such as a sound or a message: Jeg opfangede et par ord (I caught a few words). It is used mostly for signals, sounds and information.

sentence.da: Antennen kan **opfange** signaler fra satellitter langt væk.
sentence.en: The antenna can pick up signals from far-away satellites.

at opfatte.explanation: "At opfatte" means "to perceive", to take something in with your senses or to see it in a certain way. It is often how you read a person or situation: Hvordan opfatter du ham? (How do you see him?). It also means to catch words: Jeg opfattede ikke navnet (I did not catch the name).

sentence.da: Børn kan **opfatte** mere, end de voksne tror.
sentence.en: Children can perceive more than the adults think.

at opfinde.explanation: "At opfinde" means "to invent", to make something completely new that did not exist before. It also means to make up a story: Han opfandt en undskyldning (He made up an excuse).

sentence.da: Hun vil **opfinde** en maskine, som kan rydde op.
sentence.en: She wants to invent a machine that can tidy up.

at opfordre.explanation: "At opfordre" means "to urge" or "to encourage", to ask someone strongly to do something, often in public: Politiet opfordrer folk til at blive hjemme (The police urge people to stay at home). The pattern is opfordre nogen til at (urge someone to). At opmuntre (to cheer up) is about feelings and is a different word.

sentence.da: Vi vil **opfordre** alle til at stemme ved valget.
sentence.en: We want to urge everyone to vote in the election.

at opfylde.explanation: "At opfylde" means "to fulfill", to do what a promise, a hope or a rule asks for: Han opfyldte sit løfte (He kept his promise).

sentence.da: Du skal **opfylde** alle kravene, før du kan søge.
sentence.en: You must fulfill all the requirements before you can apply.

at opføre.explanation: "At opføre" means "to build" or "to perform". To build is used for larger buildings: Kommunen opfører en ny skole (The council is building a new school). To perform is used for putting on a play or a show. With sig it means "to behave": at opføre sig pænt (to behave nicely).

sentence.da: Teatret vil **opføre** et stykke af Holberg i efteråret.
sentence.en: The theater will stage a play by Holberg in the fall.

at opføre sig.explanation: "At opføre sig" means "to behave", and it needs a word like pænt (nicely) or dårligt (badly): Han opfører sig dårligt (He behaves badly). Without sig, at opføre means "to build": De opfører et hus (They are building a house).

sentence.da: Børn skal **opføre sig** pænt i skolen.
sentence.en: Children must behave nicely at school.

at opgive.explanation: "At opgive" means "to give up", to quit trying because it seems impossible or not worth it: Hun opgav at finde nøglen (She gave up looking for the key). It is also used for stating information, like at opgive et navn (to give a name).

sentence.da: Vi vil aldrig **opgive**, selv når det bliver svært.
sentence.en: We will never give up, even when it gets hard.

at opgradere.explanation: "At opgradere" means "to upgrade", to replace something with a newer or stronger version, like a phone, a program or a plan: Jeg opgraderer mit abonnement (I upgrade my subscription). It is built like the English word, with op (up) in front. For making something better in general, use at forbedre (to improve).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **opgradere** telefonen, før den bliver for langsom.
sentence.en: I want to upgrade the phone before it gets too slow.

at opgøre.explanation: "At opgøre" means "to calculate" or "to settle": to add everything up and find the final amount: opgøre regnskabet (settle the accounts), opgøre skaden (calculate the damage). It is used in business, insurance and statistics, where an official number is needed.

sentence.da: Banken kan **opgøre** gælden, så vi ved det præcise beløb.
sentence.en: The bank can calculate the debt so we know the exact amount.

at ophæve.explanation: "At ophæve" means "to repeal" or "to lift": to officially end a rule or a decision: ophæve en lov (repeal a law), ophæve en regel (lift a rule).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **ophæve** forbuddet mod at tage hunde med i parken.
sentence.en: The city will lift the ban on bringing dogs to the park.

at ophøre.explanation: "At ophøre" means "to cease", to come to an end, usually for something that has been going on: Støjen ophører klokken ti (The noise ceases at ten). It sounds official, like in letters and announcements. In everyday speech people say at holde op (to stop): Hold op! (Stop it!)

sentence.da: Ordningen kan **ophøre**, hvis ingen længere bruger den.
sentence.en: The scheme can cease if nobody uses it any more.

at opklare.explanation: "At opklare" means "to solve (a case)", to find out the truth about a crime or a mystery. It can also mean to clear up a misunderstanding: Vi må opklare, hvad der skete (We must find out what happened). For puzzles and math problems, use at løse (to solve).

sentence.da: Politiet kan **opklare** sagen, hvis nogen har set noget.
sentence.en: The police can solve the case if somebody has seen something.

at oplade.explanation: "At oplade" means "to charge", to fill a battery with power: Jeg oplader min computer (I charge my computer). In daily speech, people often drop op and say at lade: Jeg lader min telefon (I am charging my phone).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **oplade** min telefon i nat.
sentence.en: I have to charge my phone tonight.

at opleve.explanation: "At opleve" means "to experience", for things you see or that happen to you: Vi oplevede en flot solopgang (We saw a beautiful sunrise).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **opleve** Italien en dag.
sentence.en: I would like to experience Italy one day.

at oplyse.explanation: "At oplyse" means "to inform" or "to light up". To inform is to give someone facts, as in news from an authority: Politiet oplyser, at manden er fundet (The police say the man has been found). To light up is for places: Månen oplyser vejen (The moon lights up the road).

sentence.da: Kan du **oplyse**, hvornår toget kommer?
sentence.en: Can you tell me when the train comes?

at oplære.explanation: "At oplære" means "to train": to show a person how to do the practical work of a job, step by step: Butikken oplærer ham i at bruge kassen (The shop trains him to use the register). For sports and exercise, Danes say at træne (to work out) instead.

sentence.da: Hun skal **oplære** den nye medarbejder i at bruge maskinen.
sentence.en: She has to train the new employee to use the machine.

at opmuntre.explanation: "At opmuntre" means "to encourage" or "to cheer up", to give someone courage or a better mood when they feel down: Læreren opmuntrede hende til at prøve igen (The teacher encouraged her to try again). It is about feelings. To ask someone strongly to act, use at opfordre (to urge).

sentence.da: Et par rare ord kan **opmuntre** en, der er ked af det.
sentence.en: A few kind words can cheer up someone who is sad.

at opnå.explanation: "At opnå" means "to achieve", to end up with a result through effort or time: at opnå et godt resultat (to achieve a good result). It also fits things you arrive at rather than do, like a speed or a deal: at opnå enighed (to come to an agreement).

sentence.da: Hun vil **opnå** en høj karakter, fordi hun læser hver dag.
sentence.en: She wants to achieve a high grade because she studies every day.

at opprioritere.explanation: "At opprioritere" means "to prioritize higher": to make something more important than before, with more attention and funding: opprioritere ældreplejen (give elder care more attention). The op works like "up" in English.

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **opprioritere** skolerne og bruge flere penge på dem.
sentence.en: The city will give schools higher priority and spend more money on them.

at opretholde.explanation: "At opretholde" means "to maintain", to keep something going in the same state: order, peace, a standard or a contact. It fits things that would soon fail without effort: Vi må opretholde kontakten (We must keep up the contact). For cleaning and repairing a building or machine, use at vedligeholde (to keep in repair).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **opretholde** gode vaner uden en fast plan.
sentence.en: It is hard to keep up good habits without a fixed plan.

at oprette.explanation: "At oprette" means "to set up" or "to create", to make something official that did not exist before: an account, a company or a file. Jeg opretter en konto (I create an account). It is about making something exist. At opsætte (to set up) is about putting a thing in place.

sentence.da: Du skal **oprette** en bruger, før du kan logge ind.
sentence.en: You have to create a user before you can log in.

at opsige.explanation: "At opsige" means "to cancel" or "to terminate" something that runs over time, such as a job, a lease or a subscription, with notice: Jeg har opsagt min lejlighed (I have given notice on my apartment). For your own job, say opsige sin stilling (resign).

sentence.da: Du kan **opsige** abonnementet med en måneds varsel.
sentence.en: You can cancel the subscription with a month's notice.

at opstille.explanation: "At opstille" means "to set up" or "to nominate". To set up is to put things in position: Vi opstiller teltet (We set up the tent). In politics it means to put someone forward for election: Partiet opstiller Lars til valget (The party puts Lars forward for the election).

sentence.da: Vi skal **opstille** stolene i rækker, før gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: We have to set up the chairs in rows before the guests come.

at opstå.explanation: "At opstå" means "to arise" or "to occur", to come into being without anyone planning it, like a problem, a fire or a misunderstanding: Der opstod en brand (A fire broke out). It is a different word from at stå op (to get out of bed).

sentence.da: Der kan **opstå** problemer, hvis vi ikke taler sammen.
sentence.en: Problems can arise if we do not talk to each other.

at opsummere.explanation: "At opsummere" means "to summarize", to give the key parts of something in a shorter form: a meeting, a text or a discussion. People often use it at the end, to wrap things up: Lad mig lige opsummere (Let me sum it up quickly).

sentence.da: Kan du kort **opsummere**, hvad der blev sagt på mødet?
sentence.en: Can you briefly summarize what was said at the meeting?

at opsætte.explanation: "At opsætte" means "to set up", to put something in place and make it ready, like a shelf, a lamp or a program: Jeg opsætter hylden (I put up the shelf). It is about placing a thing. To make an account or a company, use at oprette (to create).

sentence.da: Det tager kort tid at **opsætte** en ny printer.
sentence.en: It takes little time to set up a new printer.

at opsøge.explanation: "At opsøge" means "to seek out", to go to a person or place on purpose, often because you need help or advice: Hun opsøgte hjælp hos naboen (She sought out help from the neighbor). You take the first step yourself, so nobody comes to you.

sentence.da: Man bør **opsøge** en læge, hvis smerterne ikke går over.
sentence.en: You should seek out a doctor if the pain does not go away.

at optage.explanation: "At optage" means "to record" sound or video: Jeg optager sangen (I am recording the song). It also means "to take up" room: Det optager meget plads (It takes up a lot of space).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **optage** sangen på min telefon.
sentence.en: I would like to record the song on my phone.

at optimere.explanation: "At optimere" means "to optimize", to make something work as well as it can, such as a process, a route or your time. It is about getting the most from what you already have. At forbedre (to improve) is the general word for making something better.

sentence.da: Man kan **optimere** en hjemmeside, så den åbner hurtigere.
sentence.en: You can optimize a website so that it opens faster.

at optrappe.explanation: "At optrappe" means "to escalate": to make something bigger or more intense step by step: optrappe indsatsen (step up the effort). It is built from op (up) and en trappe (a staircase), so it goes up one step at a time.

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **optrappe** en konflikt, hvis man vil have fred.
sentence.en: You should not escalate a conflict if you want peace.

at optræde.explanation: "At optræde" means "to perform" or "to appear". It is used for musicians and actors on stage: Bandet optræder i aften (The band is performing tonight). It also means to take part in a role, like at optræde som vidne (to appear as a witness).

sentence.da: Skuespillerne vil **optræde** i teatret hver aften i en uge.
sentence.en: The actors will perform in the theater every evening for a week.

at ordne.explanation: "At ordne" means "to fix" or "to sort out" a task or problem: Jeg ordner det (I will sort it out).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **ordne** papirerne til banken.
sentence.en: I have to sort out the papers for the bank.

at organisere.explanation: "At organisere" means "to organize", planning and arranging something: Hun organiserer en tur (She is organizing a trip). It can also mean putting things in order: Jeg organiserer mine filer (I am organizing my files).

sentence.da: Vi vil **organisere** en stor fest for hende.
sentence.en: We want to organize a big party for her.

at orientere.explanation: "At orientere" means "to inform" or "to orient". Most often you inform someone about something: Direktøren orienterer medarbejderne om planerne (The director informs the staff about the plans). With sig, at orientere sig means to look around to get your bearings.

sentence.da: Vi vil **orientere** alle om ændringerne i en mail.
sentence.en: We want to inform everyone about the changes in an email.

at orke.explanation: "At orke" means "to have the energy for", and it is mostly used in questions and with ikke (not): Jeg orker ikke mere (I can't take any more). Orker du at gå en tur? (Do you have the energy for a walk?)

forms.en: I have had the energy for

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og kan ikke **orke** at lave mad.
sentence.en: I am tired and cannot face cooking.

at overbevise.explanation: "At overbevise" means "to convince", to make someone believe or agree by giving reasons or proof. The pattern is overbevise nogen om (convince someone of). At overtale (to persuade) gets someone to do something, while overbevise changes what they believe.

sentence.da: Gode argumenter kan **overbevise** selv dem, der var imod.
sentence.en: Good arguments can convince even those who were against it.

at overdrage.explanation: "At overdrage" means "to hand over" or "to transfer", used when something official passes from one person to another, such as a company, a role or a right: overdrage ledelsen (to hand over the management). For giving someone an ordinary thing, use at give (to give).

sentence.da: Chefen vil **overdrage** firmaet til sin datter.
sentence.en: The boss will hand over the company to his daughter.

at overdrive.explanation: "At overdrive" means "to exaggerate", to say or do more than the facts or the situation call for: Du overdriver, det var kun to minutter (You are exaggerating, it was only two minutes). Over means "beyond", so the idea is going beyond what is true.

sentence.da: Han plejer at **overdrive**, når han fortæller om sine ture.
sentence.en: He tends to exaggerate when he talks about his trips.

at overføre.explanation: "At overføre" means "to transfer", to move something from one place or person to another: Jeg overfører penge til din konto (I transfer money to your account). It is also used for passing on an illness: at overføre smitte (to pass on an infection).

sentence.da: Du kan **overføre** filerne fra telefonen til computeren.
sentence.en: You can transfer the files from the phone to the computer.

at overføre penge.explanation: "At overføre penge" means "to transfer money", for example from one account to another: Hun overfører penge hver måned (She transfers money every month). You can also say at sende penge (to send money).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **overføre penge** til dig i aften.
sentence.en: I can transfer money to you tonight.

at overgive sig.explanation: "At overgive sig" means "to surrender", to stop fighting and give yourself to the other side. Sig changes with the person: jeg overgiver mig (I surrender), de overgiver sig (they surrender). It also works in play, like in a game or an argument: Jeg overgiver mig! (I give up!)

sentence.da: Soldaterne måtte **overgive sig**, fordi de ikke havde mere mad.
sentence.en: The soldiers had to surrender because they had no more food.

at overgå.explanation: "At overgå" means "to surpass", to be better or greater than someone or something. It is often used about expectations: overgå forventningerne (to exceed the expectations).

sentence.da: Hun kan **overgå** alle, fordi hun træner hver dag.
sentence.en: She can surpass everyone because she trains every day.

at overhale.explanation: "At overhale" means "to overtake", to pass a car or a bike on the road: Hun overhaler en traktor (She overtakes a tractor). To catch up with someone ahead of you, use at indhente (to catch up): Jeg indhenter dig (I catch up with you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **overhale** den langsomme bil foran os.
sentence.en: I want to overtake the slow car in front of us.

at overholde.explanation: "At overholde" means "to comply with", to do what a rule, a deadline or an agreement requires: overholde fristen (to meet the deadline). The thing you comply with comes straight after it, with no extra word.

sentence.da: Alle skal **overholde** reglerne i svømmehallen.
sentence.en: Everyone must comply with the rules in the swimming pool.

at overkomme.explanation: "At overkomme" means "to manage", to have the strength or time to get a big task done. It is mostly used with ikke: Jeg kan ikke overkomme det hele (I cannot manage it all). For beating a fear or an opponent, use at overvinde (to overcome).

sentence.da: Vi kan ikke **overkomme** så meget arbejde på én dag.
sentence.en: We cannot manage so much work in one day.

at overlade.explanation: "At overlade" means "to leave (to someone)" or "to hand over", to let another person take care of something or decide it: Jeg overlader beslutningen til dig (I leave the decision to you). It is often used with til (to), as in overlade noget til tilfældighederne (to leave something to chance).

forms.en: I have left (to someone) / handed over

sentence.da: Du kan roligt **overlade** opvasken til mig i aften.
sentence.en: You can safely leave the dishes to me tonight.

at overleve.explanation: "At overleve" means "to survive": Han overlevede ulykken (He survived the accident). It is built from over (over) and leve (to live), so it means to live through something. Leve is about being alive, so for a place use at bo (to live somewhere): Jeg bor i Odense (I live in Odense).

sentence.da: Man kan ikke **overleve** uden vand.
sentence.en: You cannot survive without water.

at overnatte.explanation: "At overnatte" means "to stay overnight", for example at a hotel, a hostel or a friend's house.

sentence.da: Vi vil **overnatte** på et hotel.
sentence.en: We want to stay overnight at a hotel.

at overraske.explanation: "At overraske" means "to surprise": Jeg vil overraske min mor (I want to surprise my mom). It also means to catch someone off guard: Regnen overraskede os (The rain surprised us).

sentence.da: Han vil **overraske** sin kone med en rejse.
sentence.en: He wants to surprise his wife with a trip.

at overrække.explanation: "At overrække" means "to present", to hand something over in person to someone, often at a ceremony: overrække en buket (to present a bouquet).

sentence.da: Borgmesteren vil **overrække** prisen til vinderen.
sentence.en: The mayor will present the prize to the winner.

at overse.explanation: "At overse" means "to overlook", to miss something by accident, like a mistake or a sign: Jeg overså fejlen (I missed the error). It can also be on purpose, when you choose not to react to something small. Do not mix it up with English oversee: at overse is to miss, not to supervise.

sentence.da: Det er let at **overse** et lille skilt i mørket.
sentence.en: It is easy to overlook a small sign in the dark.

at overskride.explanation: "At overskride" means "to exceed", to go past a limit such as a speed, a budget or a deadline: Vi har overskredet budgettet (We have gone over the budget). It is about going past a line that was meant to hold you back.

sentence.da: Du må ikke **overskride** hastighedsgrænsen på motorvejen.
sentence.en: You must not exceed the speed limit on the highway.

at overskue.explanation: "At overskue" means "to get an overview of", to see a whole situation or task clearly enough to deal with it. It is often used with ikke when something feels too big: Jeg kan ikke overskue det (It is too much for me).

forms.en: I have gotten an overview of

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **overskue** så mange opgaver på én gang.
sentence.en: I cannot get an overview of so many tasks at once.

at oversætte.explanation: "At oversætte" means "to translate": Jeg oversætter brevet (I translate the letter). Use fra (from) and til (to) for the languages: Hun oversætter fra dansk til tysk (She translates from Danish to German).

sentence.da: Kan du **oversætte** det her til engelsk?
sentence.en: Can you translate this into English?

at overtage.explanation: "At overtage" means "to take over", to receive control or responsibility from someone else: a job, a shop or a house. Kan du overtage rattet? (Can you take over the wheel?) It also fits duties: at overtage ansvaret (to take over the responsibility).

sentence.da: Min søster vil **overtage** butikken, når far går på pension.
sentence.en: My sister wants to take over the store when Dad retires.

at overtale.explanation: "At overtale" means "to persuade", getting someone to say yes: Hun overtalte mig til at komme med (She persuaded me to come along). Use til at (to) before the action.

sentence.da: Hun vil **overtale** sin chef til at give hende fri.
sentence.en: She wants to persuade her boss to give her time off.

at overtræde.explanation: "At overtræde" means "to violate", to go against a law, a rule or a limit: overtræde fartgrænsen (to break the speed limit). The opposite is at overholde (to comply with).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **overtræde** loven, og straffen kan være en bøde.
sentence.en: You must not violate the law, and the punishment can be a fine.

at overveje.explanation: "At overveje" means "to consider", which is thinking about something carefully before you decide: Jeg overvejer at flytte (I am considering moving). A quick thought is different: Jeg tænker på mad (I am thinking about food).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **overveje** tilbuddet i et par dage.
sentence.en: I will consider the offer for a couple of days.

at overvinde.explanation: "At overvinde" means "to overcome", to get past something difficult, like a problem or an opponent: Vi overvandt problemerne (We overcame the problems). Do not mix it up with at vinde (to win), which is for games and prizes.

sentence.da: Det er svært at **overvinde** frygten for at tale foran folk.
sentence.en: It is hard to overcome the fear of speaking in front of people.

at overvåge.explanation: "At overvåge" means "to monitor" or "to watch", to follow someone or something over time so you know what happens: Kameraer overvåger indgangen (Cameras monitor the entrance). It fits patients, prices and places, and the watching is close and goes on for a while.

sentence.da: Lægerne vil **overvåge** hende natten over, fordi hun har feber.
sentence.en: The doctors will monitor her through the night because she has a fever.

en oberst.explanation: "En oberst" means "a colonel", a high officer rank in the army and air force, just below en general (a general).

sentence.da: En **oberst** leder mange soldater og har en høj rang.
sentence.en: A colonel leads many soldiers and has a high rank.

en odder.explanation: "En odder" means "an otter", an animal that lives by water, swims well and has thick brown fur.

sentence.da: En **odder** svømmer godt og spiser fisk fra åen.
sentence.en: An otter swims well and eats fish from the stream.

en officer.explanation: "En officer" means "an officer", a person in the armed forces who has a leadership rank and gives orders to those under them. A police officer is en betjent instead.

sentence.da: En **officer** leder soldaterne og tager beslutninger i krig.
sentence.en: An officer leads the soldiers and makes decisions in war.

en offside.explanation: "En offside" means "an offside", when a player is too far ahead of the others when the ball is passed.

sentence.da: Der var **offside**, så målet tæller ikke.
sentence.en: It was offside, so the goal does not count.

en okse.explanation: "En okse" means "an ox", a large farm animal: a male of the cattle family that cannot have young, kept for meat or to pull heavy loads.

sentence.da: Kødet fra en **okse** hedder oksekød.
sentence.en: The meat from an ox is called beef.

en oldefar.explanation: "En oldefar" means "a great-grandfather", one generation above your grandparents.

sentence.da: Min **oldefar** er far til min farmor.
sentence.en: My great-grandfather is the father of my grandmother.

en oldemor.explanation: "En oldemor" means "a great-grandmother", one generation above your grandparents.

sentence.da: Min **oldemor** er mor til min morfar.
sentence.en: My great-grandmother is the mother of my grandfather.

en oliven.explanation: "En oliven" means "an olive", a salty fruit from a tree in warm countries. The oil from it is olivenolie (olive oil).

sentence.da: En **oliven** er lille, grøn eller sort.
sentence.en: An olive is small, green or black.

en ombudsmand.explanation: "En ombudsmand" means "an ombudsman", an independent person who listens to people who feel they were treated unfairly by the state and checks what happened. In Denmark, Folketingets Ombudsmand does this for the whole country.

sentence.da: Borgeren skrev til en **ombudsmand**, fordi staten havde behandlet hende uretfærdigt.
sentence.en: The citizen wrote to an ombudsman because the state had treated her unfairly.

en ombygning.explanation: "En ombygning" means "a remodel", when a house, shop or room is rebuilt to look or work differently. The part om- means "over again", as in at omskrive (to rewrite).

sentence.da: Vi laver en **ombygning**, fordi køkkenet er for lille.
sentence.en: We are doing a remodel because the kitchen is too small.

en ombytning.explanation: "En ombytning" means "an exchange", when one thing is swapped for another. It also covers a mix-up where two things end up in the wrong places, such as two bags taken by the wrong owners.

sentence.da: Der var en **ombytning** i lufthavnen, og jeg fik en forkert kuffert.
sentence.en: There was a mix-up at the airport, and I got the wrong suitcase.

en omgang.explanation: "En omgang" means "a round" or "a lap", one full turn of something that is repeated. It is also used for drinks for a group: Jeg giver en omgang (I am buying a round).

sentence.da: En **omgang** rundt om banen er 400 meter lang.
sentence.en: One lap around the track is 400 meters long.

en omgangskreds.explanation: "En omgangskreds" means "a circle of friends", the people you spend time with regularly, from close ones to people you only know a little. It comes from at omgås (to spend time with).

sentence.da: Min **omgangskreds** består mest af kolleger og naboer.
sentence.en: My circle of friends mostly consists of colleagues and neighbors.

en omkamp.explanation: "En omkamp" means "a rematch", a match played again, for example after a draw. Om at the start of a word often means "again": at lave om (to redo).

sentence.da: Kampen sluttede uafgjort, og der bliver en **omkamp** på lørdag.
sentence.en: The match ended in a draw, and there will be a rematch on Saturday.

en omkostning.explanation: "En omkostning" means "a cost", money spent to run or do something, and it is mostly used in the plural. A pris (price) is what you pay for something you buy; omkostninger are running costs like repairs and insurance.

sentence.da: Opvarmning er den største **omkostning** ved at have et hus.
sentence.en: Heating is the biggest cost of owning a house.

en omkørsel.explanation: "En omkørsel" means "a detour", the route set up when a road is closed. A longer way that you choose yourself is en omvej (a roundabout way).

sentence.da: Vi må tage en **omkørsel**, fordi vejen er lukket.
sentence.en: We have to take a detour because the road is closed.

en omlægning.explanation: "En omlægning" means "a restructuring", changing how something is arranged or done, such as a tax system, a route or a company. It is also used for loans: omlægning af lån (switching a loan to new terms).

sentence.da: Regeringen planlægger en **omlægning** af skattesystemet næste år.
sentence.en: The government is planning a restructuring of the tax system next year.

en omstilling.explanation: "En omstilling" means "an adjustment" or "a transition", moving from one way of working or living to another. At a company, omstillingen is also the main phone line that connects you to the right person.

sentence.da: Skiftet til grøn energi kræver en stor **omstilling** i samfundet.
sentence.en: The shift to green energy requires a big transition in society.

en omstændighed.explanation: "En omstændighed" means "a circumstance", a fact around an event that affects how it turns out. Under alle omstændigheder means "in any case": Jeg kommer under alle omstændigheder (I will come in any case).

sentence.da: Politiet skal undersøge hver **omstændighed** ved ulykken.
sentence.en: The police must investigate every circumstance of the accident.

en omsætning.explanation: "En omsætning" means "a turnover" or "revenue", the total money a business takes in from selling, before costs are taken out. It is not the same as profit, which is fortjeneste.

sentence.da: Butikkens **omsætning** er alle pengene fra salget i en måned.
sentence.en: The store's revenue is all the money from sales in a month.

en omvej.explanation: "En omvej" means "a detour", a longer way around. It is the opposite of en genvej (a shortcut).

sentence.da: Det er en **omvej**, fordi vejen går udenom byen.
sentence.en: It is a detour because the road goes around the town.

en onkel.explanation: "En onkel" means "an uncle". Before a name it works as a title: onkel Peter (Uncle Peter).

sentence.da: Min **onkel** er min fars bror.
sentence.en: My uncle is my father's brother.

en opdagelse.explanation: "En opdagelse" means "a discovery", learning about something nobody knew before, or noticing something for the first time. It is not the same as en opfindelse (an invention): a discovery was already there, but an invention is made.

sentence.da: Penicillin var en vigtig **opdagelse** inden for medicin.
sentence.en: Penicillin was an important discovery in medicine.

en opdatering.explanation: "En opdatering" means "an update", a new version of an app or system. The action is at opdatere (to update).

sentence.da: Min telefon skal have en **opdatering** i aften.
sentence.en: My phone needs an update tonight.

en opdeling.explanation: "En opdeling" means "a division", splitting something into parts or groups. It comes from at dele op (to split up).

sentence.da: En **opdeling** af klassen i små hold gør arbejdet nemmere.
sentence.en: A division of the class into small teams makes the work easier.

en opdragelse.explanation: "En opdragelse" means "an upbringing", the way a child is taught manners and values by the adults around it. It is about what they do; en opvækst (the years of growing up in a place) is about the setting.

sentence.da: God **opdragelse** handler om at lære børn at være høflige.
sentence.en: Good upbringing is about teaching children to be polite.

en opera.explanation: "En opera" means "an opera", and also the building where it is shown: Vi skal i operaen i aften (We are going to the opera tonight). It is different from et teater (a theater), where people mostly speak.

sentence.da: I en **opera** synger sangerne hele aftenen.
sentence.en: In an opera the singers sing all evening.

en operation.explanation: "En operation" means "an operation" or "surgery" at a hospital. The action is at operere (to operate).

sentence.da: Hun skal have en **operation** på sygehuset i morgen.
sentence.en: She is having an operation at the hospital tomorrow.

en opfattelse.explanation: "En opfattelse" means "a view" or "a perception", how you see something, and it is often used for what you think about a matter: Efter min opfattelse er det for dyrt (In my view, it is too expensive).

sentence.da: Hans **opfattelse** af sagen er en helt anden end min.
sentence.en: His view of the matter is completely different from mine.

en opfindelse.explanation: "En opfindelse" means "an invention", something new that a person has made, like a machine. Unlike en opdagelse (a discovery), it did not exist before.

sentence.da: Telefonen var en stor **opfindelse**, og den ændrede verden.
sentence.en: The telephone was a great invention, and it changed the world.

en opfinder.explanation: "En opfinder" means "an inventor", a person who thinks up something new and builds it. The word comes from at opfinde (to invent), and -er makes it the person who does it, just like en lærer (a teacher).

sentence.da: En **opfinder** får ofte patent på en ny maskine.
sentence.en: An inventor often gets a patent on a new machine.

en opfordring.explanation: "En opfordring" means "a call" or "an appeal", when someone encourages others to do something. It is stronger than a plain question but not a command. På opfordring (when asked to) is common: Han sang på opfordring (He sang when asked to).

sentence.da: Der kom en **opfordring** om at spare på vandet.
sentence.en: There was a call to save water.

en opførelse.explanation: "En opførelse" means "a construction", the putting up of something large, such as a bridge. It also means a performance of a theater piece or an opera. Do not mix it up with en opførsel (behavior).

sentence.da: En **opførelse** af en stor bro kræver mange mennesker og penge.
sentence.en: The construction of a big bridge takes many people and money.

en opgang.explanation: "En opgang" means "a stairwell" or "an entrance", one entrance with its stairs in a large residential building. Big buildings often have several, named by letter or number.

sentence.da: Hver **opgang** har sin egen dør og sin egen trappe.
sentence.en: Each stairwell has its own door and its own stairs.

en opgave.explanation: "En opgave" means "a task", at work or at school. In school it can also be an exercise: en matematikopgave (a math exercise).

sentence.da: Min **opgave** er at ringe til kunderne.
sentence.en: My task is to call the customers.

en opgavebog.explanation: "En opgavebog" means "an exercise book", a book full of tasks to solve, used in school for subjects like math or language. It is for practice, so you write the answers right in it.

sentence.da: Vi løser matematiske opgaver i en **opgavebog**.
sentence.en: We solve math problems in an exercise book.

en opgivelse.explanation: "En opgivelse" means "a giving up", the act of stopping a goal or plan because you no longer think it can succeed. It comes from at opgive (to give up).

sentence.da: Hendes **opgivelse** af drømmen kom efter mange år uden held.
sentence.en: Her giving up of the dream came after many years without luck.

en opgørelse.explanation: "En opgørelse" means "a statement" or "a count", a written summary of figures after adding things up. It comes from at gøre op (to settle up).

sentence.da: Banken sender mig en **opgørelse** over alle mine indtægter og udgifter.
sentence.en: The bank sends me a statement of all my income and expenses.

en opholdstilladelse.explanation: "En opholdstilladelse" means "a residence permit", an official paper from the authorities that lets a foreigner live in a country. It is built from ophold (a stay) and tilladelse (a permission), so literally stay permission.

sentence.da: Hun fik en **opholdstilladelse**, så hun kunne bo i Danmark.
sentence.en: She got a residence permit so she could live in Denmark.

en ophævelse.explanation: "En ophævelse" means "an abolition" or "a cancellation", officially ending something that was in force, such as a rule, a contract or a ban. It comes from at ophæve (to repeal).

sentence.da: Flertallet stemte for **ophævelse** af den gamle regel.
sentence.en: The majority voted for the repeal of the old rule.

en oplader.explanation: "En oplader" means "a charger" for a phone or laptop. The action is at oplade (to charge).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **oplader**, når telefonens batteri er tomt.
sentence.en: I use a charger when the phone's battery is empty.

en oplevelse.explanation: "En oplevelse" means "an experience", something you live through. For work experience or skills, use erfaring (experience).

sentence.da: Turen til Italien var en stor **oplevelse**.
sentence.en: The trip to Italy was a great experience.

en oplysning.explanation: "En oplysning" means "a piece of information", one fact you are told. On forms, oplysninger (details) means your name, address and so on.

sentence.da: Hun gav mig en vigtig **oplysning** om prisen.
sentence.en: She gave me an important piece of information about the price.

en opmuntring.explanation: "En opmuntring" means "an encouragement", something that cheers you up or gives you courage to keep going. A small gift can also be en lille opmuntring (a little pick-me-up).

sentence.da: Et par venlige ord kan være en stor **opmuntring**, når man er trist.
sentence.en: A few kind words can be a great encouragement when you are sad.

en opposition.explanation: "En opposition" means "an opposition", in politics the groups that are not in power and question those who are. It can also mean any strong objection: Der er stærk opposition mod planen (There is strong opposition to the plan).

sentence.da: Partier i **opposition** kritiserer ofte regeringen.
sentence.en: Parties in opposition often criticize the government.

en oprindelse.explanation: "En oprindelse" means "an origin", the place or cause where something starts. It is often used for where people, words or products come from: Hvad er ordets oprindelse? (What is the origin of the word?)

sentence.da: Maden har sin **oprindelse** i Italien, men den spises overalt.
sentence.en: The food has its origin in Italy, but it is eaten everywhere.

en opringning.explanation: "En opringning" means "a phone call", the moment someone phones you or you phone someone. It is built from at ringe op (literally to ring up).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **opringning** fra banken i går.
sentence.en: I got a phone call from the bank yesterday.

en oprydning.explanation: "En oprydning" means "a tidying up", putting a room or place back in order. It is also used for clearing up after a storm or an event: oprydning efter stormen (cleanup after the storm).

sentence.da: Efter festen var der en stor **oprydning** i stuen.
sentence.en: After the party there was a big cleanup in the living room.

en opsang.explanation: "En opsang" means "a telling-off", a stern talking-to after someone did something wrong, usually from a parent or a boss. You use it with få (get) and give (give): at få en opsang (to get told off).

sentence.da: Min mor gav mig en **opsang**, fordi jeg kom for sent hjem.
sentence.en: My mother gave me a telling-off because I came home too late.

en opsigelse.explanation: "En opsigelse" means "a resignation" or "a notice of termination", the formal step that ends a job, rental or subscription. It works both ways: you can hand one in yourself, or your employer can give you one. Få en opsigelse (to be let go) is the second case.

sentence.da: Hun afleverede sin **opsigelse**, fordi hun fik et nyt job.
sentence.en: She handed in her resignation because she got a new job.

en opskrift.explanation: "En opskrift" means "a recipe", a list of ingredients and steps for making a dish. The food comes after på (for): en opskrift på pandekager (a recipe for pancakes).

sentence.da: Jeg følger en **opskrift**, når jeg bager brød.
sentence.en: I follow a recipe when I bake bread.

en opslagstavle.explanation: "En opslagstavle" means "a bulletin board", a board where people pin notes and notices.

sentence.da: Jeg hængte en plakat op på en **opslagstavle**.
sentence.en: I hung a poster on a bulletin board.

en opsparing.explanation: "En opsparing" means "savings", money you have put aside over time. Danish uses the singular for the whole amount: Jeg har en lille opsparing (I have a small amount put away).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger penge til side hver måned, og det er min **opsparing**.
sentence.en: I put money aside every month, and that is my savings.

en optagelse.explanation: "En optagelse" means "a recording", sound or video saved so you can play it again later. It also means "admission" when you are accepted into a school or club: optagelse på universitetet (admission to the university).

sentence.da: Jeg lavede en **optagelse** af koncerten med min telefon.
sentence.en: I made a recording of the concert with my phone.

en optiker.explanation: "En optiker" means "an optician", a person who tests your sight and sells you glasses. An eye doctor is en øjenlæge, who treats eye diseases.

sentence.da: Jeg bestilte tid hos en **optiker**, fordi jeg ikke kunne se tavlen.
sentence.en: I booked an appointment with an optician because I could not see the board.

en optikerforretning.explanation: "En optikerforretning" means "an optician's shop", where you buy glasses and get your eyes tested.

sentence.da: Hun køber nye briller i en **optikerforretning**.
sentence.en: She buys new glasses in an optician's shop.

en optræden.explanation: "En optræden" means "a performance", when someone appears in front of an audience, such as a singer, actor or comedian. It can also mean how a person comes across in public: Hendes optræden var rolig og sikker (She came across as calm and confident).

sentence.da: Bandets **optræden** på festivalen varede en hel time.
sentence.en: The band's performance at the festival lasted a whole hour.

en optælling.explanation: "En optælling" means "a count", counting things to find out how many there are, for example goods in stock or people at an event. It comes from at tælle op (to count up).

sentence.da: Efter valget foretager de en **optælling** af stemmerne.
sentence.en: After the election they carry out a count of the votes.

en opvarmning.explanation: "En opvarmning" means "a warm-up", light exercise before sport to prepare the body. It also means the heating of a building: opvarmning af huset (heating the house).

sentence.da: Spillerne laver en **opvarmning** på banen før kampen.
sentence.en: The players do a warm-up on the field before the match.

en opvask.explanation: "En opvask" means "dishwashing", the dirty dishes or the job of washing them. It is also the start of en opvaskemaskine (a dishwasher).

sentence.da: Efter middagen står der meget **opvask** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: After dinner there are lots of dishes in the kitchen.

en opvaskebørste.explanation: "En opvaskebørste" means "a dish brush", a brush with a handle for scrubbing plates and pots.

sentence.da: Jeg skrubber gryden med en **opvaskebørste**.
sentence.en: I scrub the pot with a dish brush.

en opvaskemaskine.explanation: "En opvaskemaskine" means "a dishwasher", the machine in a kitchen that cleans plates and cups with hot water. The person who does the job is en opvasker (a dishwasher person).

sentence.da: Vi sætter snavsede tallerkener i en **opvaskemaskine**.
sentence.en: We put dirty plates in a dishwasher.

en opvasker.explanation: "En opvasker" means "a dishwasher" when it is a person, someone who washes dishes in a restaurant. The machine is en opvaskemaskine (a dishwashing machine).

sentence.da: Som **opvasker** vasker han tallerkener hver aften.
sentence.en: As a dishwasher he washes plates every evening.

en opvækst.explanation: "En opvækst" means "an upbringing", the early years of your life and what they were like. It is about the setting you were raised in; en opdragelse (the manners your parents taught you) is about what they did.

sentence.da: Hendes **opvækst** på landet var rolig, og hun havde mange dyr.
sentence.en: Her upbringing in the country was calm, and she had many animals.

en ordbog.explanation: "En ordbog" means "a dictionary", built from ord (word) and bog (book). The same ord is in et ordsprog (a proverb).

sentence.da: Jeg slår ordet op i en **ordbog**.
sentence.en: I look the word up in a dictionary.

en ordliste.explanation: "En ordliste" means "a word list" or "a glossary", a list of words with their meanings, often made for learners of a language or a school subject. It is shorter and simpler than en ordbog (a dictionary).

sentence.da: Bagest i bogen er der en **ordliste** med de svære ord.
sentence.en: At the back of the book is a word list with the hard words.

en ordning.explanation: "En ordning" means "an arrangement" or "a scheme", a fixed way of organizing something, at work, at home or by the state. It comes from at ordne (to put in order) and often ends other words: en pensionsordning (a pension scheme).

sentence.da: Vi har en fast **ordning**: Mor handler, og far laver mad.
sentence.en: We have a fixed arrangement: Mom shops, and Dad cooks.

en ordre.explanation: "En ordre" means "an order", something you are told to do by someone with authority, like a boss. It also means a customer's order of goods in business: en ordre på ti stole (an order for ten chairs). In a restaurant, Danes use at bestille (to order) instead.

sentence.da: Soldaterne skal følge hver **ordre** fra deres chef.
sentence.en: The soldiers must follow every order from their boss.

en organisation.explanation: "En organisation" means "an organization", a group of people working together for a shared aim, such as a charity. It can also mean how something is arranged: organisationen af arbejdet (the way the work is arranged).

sentence.da: Røde Kors er en **organisation** og hjælper mennesker over hele verden.
sentence.en: The Red Cross is an organization and helps people all over the world.

en orkan.explanation: "En orkan" means "a hurricane", a violent wind of extreme force. In Danish weather reports, it is the very top level of wind strength.

sentence.da: Under en **orkan** vælter vinden træer og skader huse.
sentence.en: During a hurricane the wind knocks over trees and damages houses.

en orm.explanation: "En orm" means "a worm", the long soft animal that lives in the soil. Fishermen use it as bait.

sentence.da: Fuglen finder en **orm** i græsset.
sentence.en: The bird finds a worm in the grass.

en ostehandler.explanation: "En ostehandler" means "a cheesemonger", a person or shop that sells cheese.

sentence.da: Jeg køber ost hos en **ostehandler** i byen.
sentence.en: I buy cheese from a cheesemonger in town.

en ostemad.explanation: "En ostemad" means "a cheese sandwich", a slice of bread with cheese on it. It is ost (cheese) plus mad (food). Mad alone means food, but en mad is also a sandwich, as in en madpakke (a packed lunch).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg en **ostemad** og et æble.
sentence.en: For lunch I eat a cheese sandwich and an apple.

en osteskærer.explanation: "En osteskærer" means "a cheese slicer", the flat tool that cuts thin, even slices from a block of cheese.

sentence.da: Jeg skærer osten med en **osteskærer**.
sentence.en: I cut the cheese with a cheese slicer.

en overbetjent.explanation: "En overbetjent" means "a senior police officer", a higher rank within the police. The over- means higher in rank, like in en overlæge (a senior doctor).

sentence.da: Han blev **overbetjent** efter mange år ved politiet.
sentence.en: He became a senior police officer after many years with the police.

en overbevisning.explanation: "En overbevisning" means "a conviction", an idea you hold very firmly, often about politics, religion or right and wrong. A conviction in court is something else: en domfældelse (a guilty verdict).

sentence.da: Af **overbevisning** spiser han aldrig kød.
sentence.en: Out of conviction, he never eats meat.

en overdosis.explanation: "En overdosis" means "an overdose", a dose of a drug or medicine that is too large and can harm the body. The over- often means "too much", as in at overvurdere (to overestimate).

sentence.da: Han fik en **overdosis**, fordi han tog for mange piller.
sentence.en: He had an overdose because he took too many pills.

en overenskomst.explanation: "En overenskomst" means "a collective agreement", a deal between employers and a trade union that sets wages and rules for a whole group of workers. It applies on top of what you agree with your own employer, and many jobs in Denmark are covered by one.

sentence.da: Lønnen og arbejdstiden for alle ansatte står i en **overenskomst**.
sentence.en: The pay and working hours for all employees are in a collective agreement.

en overflade.explanation: "En overflade" means "a surface", the outside of something, such as the top of water. It is built from over (over) and flade (flat area). Flade goes with flad (flat), as in en fladskærm (a flat-screen TV).

sentence.da: Bordet har en meget glat **overflade**.
sentence.en: The table has a very smooth surface.

en overførsel.explanation: "En overførsel" means "a transfer", moving something from one place to another, most often money between bank accounts. It can also be data: overførsel af filer (transfer of files).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler huslejen med en **overførsel** hver måned.
sentence.en: I pay the rent with a transfer every month.

en overgang.explanation: "En overgang" means "a transition", the move from one stage to another, such as from winter to spring. Over- means "across", so it is literally a going across, and the same word is used for a crossing: en fodgængerovergang (a pedestrian crossing).

sentence.da: Det er en stor **overgang** at skifte fra skole til arbejde.
sentence.en: It is a big transition to change from school to work.

en overnatning.explanation: "En overnatning" means "an overnight stay", a stay where you sleep away from home, for example at a hotel.

sentence.da: Hvad koster en **overnatning** på hotellet?
sentence.en: What does an overnight stay at the hotel cost?

en overraskelse.explanation: "En overraskelse" means "a surprise", something you did not expect. The action is at overraske (to surprise).

sentence.da: Din gave var en dejlig **overraskelse**.
sentence.en: Your gift was a lovely surprise.

en oversigt.explanation: "En oversigt" means "an overview", a short summary that shows the main points.

sentence.da: Læreren giver os en **oversigt** over kurset.
sentence.en: The teacher gives us an overview of the course.

en overskrift.explanation: "En overskrift" means "a headline", the big title above a news story. It is also the line at the top of a document or a chapter: Skriv en overskrift øverst på siden (Write a headline at the top of the page).

sentence.da: Avisen har en stor **overskrift** på forsiden.
sentence.en: The newspaper has a big headline on the front page.

en oversvømmelse.explanation: "En oversvømmelse" means "a flood", when water covers land or buildings that are normally dry, after heavy rain or when a river or the sea rises. It can also be a small flood at home, such as from a burst pipe.

sentence.da: Efter det kraftige regn kom der en **oversvømmelse** i kælderen.
sentence.en: After the heavy rain there was a flood in the basement.

en oversættelse.explanation: "En oversættelse" means "a translation", a written text moved from one language into another. A person who does this out loud with speech is en tolk (an interpreter).

sentence.da: Bogen kom i en **oversættelse** fra engelsk til dansk.
sentence.en: The book came out in a translation from English to Danish.

en oversætter.explanation: "En oversætter" means "a translator", a person who turns written text from one language into another.

sentence.da: Min ven er **oversætter** og arbejder med mange sprog.
sentence.en: My friend is a translator and works with many languages.

en overvejelse.explanation: "En overvejelse" means "a consideration", thinking about something carefully before you decide. It is often used in the plural: efter nogle overvejelser (after some thought).

sentence.da: Det kræver en grundig **overvejelse**, når man vælger uddannelse.
sentence.en: It takes careful consideration when you choose what to study.

en ovn.explanation: "En ovn" means "an oven", the one you bake and roast in. Typical phrases are i ovnen (in the oven) and at tænde ovnen (to turn on the oven). The cooking surface on top is a different word, en kogeplade (a stovetop).

sentence.da: Jeg bager en kage i en varm **ovn**.
sentence.en: I am baking a cake in a hot oven.

et offentligt rum.explanation: "Et offentligt rum" means "a public space", a place that anyone can enter, like a street, a park or a library. You often hear it as i det offentlige rum (in public space), meaning out where everyone can see you.

forms.da: offentlige rum er åbne for alle
forms.en: public spaces are open to everyone

sentence.da: Et **offentligt rum** er et sted, som alle må bruge.
sentence.en: A public space is a place that everyone may use.

et offentligt toilet.explanation: "Et offentligt toilet" means "a public restroom". On signs, you may see et herretoilet (a men's restroom) or et dametoilet (a women's restroom).

forms.da: Er der et offentligt toilet her?
forms.en: Is there a public restroom here?

sentence.da: Der er et **offentligt toilet** i parken.
sentence.en: There is a public restroom in the park.

et offer.explanation: "Et offer" means "a victim", for example of a crime or an accident: Politiet talte med offeret (The police spoke with the victim). It also means "a sacrifice": Det kræver et offer (It takes a sacrifice).

sentence.da: Politiet hjalp et **offer** efter ulykken.
sentence.en: The police helped a victim after the accident.

et omdømme.explanation: "Et omdømme" means "a reputation", what people in general think of a person, a company or a place. It is built up over time from what people hear and experience.

sentence.da: Firmaet har et godt **omdømme**, fordi kunderne er glade.
sentence.en: The company has a good reputation because the customers are happy.

et omklædningsrum.explanation: "Et omklædningsrum" means "a locker room", a room at a gym, pool or sports club where you change clothes. Its first part, omklædning, means changing clothes.

sentence.da: Der er skabe og bænke i et **omklædningsrum**.
sentence.en: There are lockers and benches in a locker room.

et område.explanation: "Et område" means "an area", a part of a place. It also means a field of knowledge: Hun er ekspert på dette område (She is an expert in this field).

sentence.da: Der er mange parker i dette **område**.
sentence.en: There are many parks in this area.

et ophold.explanation: "Et ophold" means "a stay", the time you spend somewhere, such as in a hotel. It also fits a short stop on a trip: et kort ophold (a short stop).

sentence.da: Vi havde et dejligt **ophold** på hotellet.
sentence.en: We had a lovely stay at the hotel.

et opholdsrum.explanation: "Et opholdsrum" means "a lounge" or "a common room", a room where people can sit and relax together, for example at a school, a workplace or a care home. Its first part comes from at opholde sig (to stay somewhere).

sentence.da: Eleverne kan hvile sig og snakke sammen i et **opholdsrum**.
sentence.en: The students can rest and talk together in a common room.

et opkald.explanation: "Et opkald" means "a phone call" as an event, the moment the phone rings or you dial. The talk itself is en samtale (a conversation): Vi havde en lang samtale (We had a long conversation).

sentence.da: Jeg fik et **opkald** fra skolen i dag.
sentence.en: I got a call from the school today.

et opkøb.explanation: "Et opkøb" means "an acquisition" and "a buyout", when a company buys another company or a large part of it. It comes from at købe op (to buy up), where op adds the idea of buying something up completely.

sentence.da: Firmaet fik en ny ejer efter et **opkøb**.
sentence.en: The company got a new owner after an acquisition.

et oplæg.explanation: "Et oplæg" means "a presentation" and "a proposal": a short talk or a written plan that starts a conversation. It is common at work and at school, where one person starts and the group continues.

sentence.da: Hun holder et kort **oplæg**, og så diskuterer vi det.
sentence.en: She gives a short presentation, and then we discuss it.

et oprør.explanation: "Et oprør" means "a rebellion" and "an uprising", when many people openly rise up against those in power. It is also used on a small scale: Børnene gjorde oprør mod reglerne (The children rebelled against the rules).

sentence.da: Der var **oprør** i byen, og folk krævede en ny leder.
sentence.en: There was an uprising in the city, and people demanded a new leader.

et opslag.explanation: "Et opslag" means "a post" on social media: Hun skrev et opslag om sin ferie (She wrote a post about her vacation). It also means a notice on a board, like et opslag på skolen (a notice at the school).

sentence.da: Hun delte et **opslag** om sin nye bog.
sentence.en: She shared a post about her new book.

et optog.explanation: "Et optog" means "a parade", a group of people walking together through the streets, often with music or flags. It is used for cheerful events, such as a carnival, and for serious ones, such as a protest.

sentence.da: Et **optog** med musik og flag gik gennem byens gader.
sentence.en: A parade with music and flags went through the streets of the town.

et ord.explanation: "Et ord" means "a word". Hvad betyder det ord? means "What does that word mean?". A dictionary is en ordbog, literally a word book.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke finde det **ord** i ordbogen.
sentence.en: I cannot find that word in the dictionary.

et ordforråd.explanation: "Et ordforråd" means "a vocabulary", all the words a person knows and uses. It is built from ord (word) and forråd (a stock of supplies), so it is literally a stock of words. You say that someone has et stort ordforråd (a large vocabulary).

sentence.da: Børn lærer mange nye ord og får et større **ordforråd**.
sentence.en: Children learn many new words and get a bigger vocabulary.

et ordspil.explanation: "Et ordspil" means "a pun" and "wordplay", a clever phrase that plays on words that sound alike or have two meanings. It is built from et ord (a word) and et spil (a game), so it is literally a word game.

sentence.da: Det er et **ordspil**, fordi ordet har to betydninger.
sentence.en: It is a pun, because the word has two meanings.

et ordsprog.explanation: "Et ordsprog" means "a proverb", a short, well-known statement of advice about life. One example is Den, der intet vover, intet vinder (Nothing ventured, nothing gained).

sentence.da: Et gammelt **ordsprog** siger, at øvelse gør mester.
sentence.en: An old proverb says that practice makes perfect.

et organ.explanation: "Et organ" means "an organ", a part of the body with its own job. The liver, the kidneys and the lungs are organs.

sentence.da: Hjertet er et **organ**, som pumper blodet rundt i kroppen.
sentence.en: The heart is an organ that pumps the blood around the body.

et overblik.explanation: "Et overblik" means "an overview", a clear picture of the whole situation without the small details. You often lose it: Jeg har mistet overblikket (I have lost track of things). To gain it, say at få overblik (to get an overview).

related.en: a list of the main points

sentence.da: Kortet giver mig et godt **overblik** over hele byen.
sentence.en: The map gives me a good overview of the whole city.

et overfald.explanation: "Et overfald" means "an assault", a sudden violent act against a person, usually by someone who surprises them. If the person who did it also steals something, it is called et røveri (a robbery).

sentence.da: Politiet efterforsker et **overfald**, der skete på gaden i nat.
sentence.en: The police are investigating an assault that happened on the street last night.

et overskud.explanation: "Et overskud" means "a surplus", more than what is needed. For a company, it is the money left after all costs, which is profit. For a person, at have overskud means having energy to spare: Jeg har ikke overskud i dag (I do not have the energy today).

sentence.da: Firmaet havde et stort **overskud** sidste år.
sentence.en: The company had a large surplus last year.

et overskæg.explanation: "Et overskæg" means "a mustache", the hair that grows on the upper lip. Do not mix it up with et skæg (a beard), which grows on the chin and cheeks.

sentence.da: Han har et **overskæg** lige under næsen.
sentence.en: He has a mustache right under his nose.

objektiv.explanation: "Objektiv" means "objective", based on facts and not on personal feelings. Et objektiv is also the lens of a camera: Han skiftede objektiv (He changed the lens).

sentence.da: Journalisten beskriver bare fakta og er helt **objektiv**.
sentence.en: The journalist just describes the facts and is completely objective.

obligatorisk.explanation: "Obligatorisk" means "mandatory", made necessary by a rule and not by your own choice. It is often said about classes, tests and insurance.

sentence.da: Mødet er **obligatorisk**, og alle skal komme.
sentence.en: The meeting is mandatory and everyone must come.

odds.explanation: "Odds" means "odds", the numbers in gambling that show how much you can earn for each krone you put in. The lower the number, the more likely the result.

sentence.da: Holdet har lave **odds**, fordi alle tror, det vinder.
sentence.en: The team has low odds because everyone thinks it will win.

offentlig.explanation: "Offentlig" means "public" and describes things that belong to everyone, such as the country or a town. The opposite is privat (private).

sentence.da: En **offentlig** skole er gratis for alle.
sentence.en: A public school is free for everyone.

offentlighed.explanation: "En offentlighed" means "the public": all the people in a country seen as one group. It also means openness: a meeting held med offentlighed (with the public present) is open, so anyone can watch it or read about it.

sentence.da: Retsmødet blev holdt uden **offentlighed**, så kun parterne var til stede.
sentence.en: The court hearing was held without the public, so only the parties were present.

offentligt.explanation: "Offentligt" means "publicly", in front of everyone and not in private. It comes from offentlig (public).

sentence.da: Politikeren sagde **offentligt** undskyld i fjernsynet.
sentence.en: The politician said sorry publicly on television.

officiel.explanation: "Officiel" means "official", for what comes from the government or from someone with the power to decide.

sentence.da: Det er en **officiel** meddelelse fra kommunen.
sentence.en: It is an official notice from the municipality.

officielt.explanation: "Officielt" means "officially", by the rules or the authorities, and it often hints that reality is different: Officielt er det forbudt, men alle gør det (Officially it is forbidden, but everyone does it).

sentence.da: Hotellet åbner **officielt** i morgen, men gæster kommer allerede.
sentence.en: The hotel opens officially tomorrow, but guests are already coming.

offline.explanation: "Offline" means "offline", not connected to the web. It is the same word as in English.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke søge, fordi min telefon er **offline**.
sentence.en: I cannot search because my phone is offline.

ofte.explanation: "Ofte" means "often". Compare Jeg går ofte i skoven (I often walk in the forest) with Jeg går aldrig i skoven (I never walk in the forest). To ask, say Hvor ofte træner du? (How often do you work out?).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **ofte** ude.
sentence.en: We often eat out.

oftest.explanation: "Oftest" means "most often" and describes what happens in most cases. It comes from ofte (often): ofte, oftere (more often), oftest.

forms.en: It most often happens in the evening

sentence.da: Jeg tager **oftest** bussen.
sentence.en: I most often take the bus.

og.explanation: "Og" means "and". Do not mix it up with også (also, too): Jeg kan også lide te (I also like tea). Og sounds like a short o, with no g sound.

sentence.da: Jeg kan lide kaffe **og** te.
sentence.en: I like coffee and tea.

også.explanation: "Også" means "also" or "too". Compare Jeg kommer også (I am coming too) with Jeg kommer heller ikke (I am not coming either). Do not mix it up with og (and): te og kaffe (tea and coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **også** have kaffe.
sentence.en: I also want coffee.

okay.explanation: "Okay" means "okay", the same word as in English. You use it to agree or to show you understand.

sentence.da: Vi ses klokken fem. – **Okay**!
sentence.en: See you at five. – Okay!

okay så.explanation: "Okay så" means "okay then" and you say it to accept what was said, or to start the next step. You are agreeing and moving on, not asking a question.

sentence.da: **Okay så**, vi mødes klokken otte.
sentence.en: Okay then, we'll meet at eight.

oksekød.explanation: "Oksekød" means "beef". It is made from okse (ox) and kød (meat), so it is literally ox meat. Kød on its own means any kind of meat.

sentence.da: Burgeren er lavet af **oksekød**.
sentence.en: The burger is made of beef.

oktober.explanation: "Oktober" means "October". Danish spells it with a k, where English has a c. Like all month names, it is written with a small letter.

sentence.da: Efter september kommer **oktober**.
sentence.en: After September comes October.

oldnordisk.explanation: "Oldnordisk" means "Old Norse", the language of the Viking Age. The Scandinavian languages all developed from it. It is also the name of a university subject, as in at læse oldnordisk (to study Old Norse).

sentence.da: Vikingerne talte **oldnordisk**, og de gamle sagaer er skrevet på sproget.
sentence.en: The Vikings spoke Old Norse, and the old sagas are written in the language.

olie.explanation: "Olie" means "oil". Put the kind in front to name it: rapsolie (rapeseed oil), olivenolie (olive oil).

sentence.da: Jeg steger kødet i **olie**.
sentence.en: I fry the meat in oil.

olivenolie.explanation: "Olivenolie" means "olive oil", built from oliven (olive) and olie (oil). It is used for salad or frying.

sentence.da: Jeg steger fisken i **olivenolie**.
sentence.en: I fry the fish in olive oil.

om.explanation: "Om" means "about", in (time from now) or "if". En bog om Danmark means "a book about Denmark". Om en uge means "in a week", unlike i en uge (for a week). And "Jeg ved ikke, om han kommer" means "I do not know if he is coming".

sentence.da: Filmen starter **om** en time.
sentence.en: The film starts in an hour.

om aftenen.explanation: "Om aftenen" means "in the evening", for something you do again and again. Compare Jeg læser om aftenen (I read in the evening, every evening) with Jeg læser i aften (I will read this evening, just today).

forms.en: In the evening we watch TV.
What do you do in the evening?

sentence.da: Vi ser tv **om aftenen**.
sentence.en: We watch TV in the evening.

om lidt.explanation: "Om lidt" means "in a little while" or "soon". Compare Jeg kommer nu (I am coming now) with Jeg kommer om lidt (I am coming in a little while).

forms.en: I am coming in a little while.
See you in a little while.

sentence.da: Maden er klar **om lidt**.
sentence.en: The food will be ready in a little while.

om morgenen.explanation: "Om morgenen" means "in the morning", for something you do again and again. Compare Jeg drikker kaffe om morgenen (I drink coffee in the morning, every morning) with Jeg drak kaffe i morges (I drank coffee this morning, just today).

forms.en: I get up in the morning.
In the morning I drink coffee.

sentence.da: Jeg står op klokken seks **om morgenen**.
sentence.en: I get up at six in the morning.

om natten.explanation: "Om natten" means "at night", for something that happens every night. Compare Jeg sover om natten (I sleep at night) with Jeg sov dårligt i nat (I slept badly last night).

sentence.da: Alle sover **om natten**.
sentence.en: Everyone sleeps at night.

om ugen.explanation: "Om ugen" means "per week" and tells how often something happens. The same pattern works for other times: to gange om dagen (twice a day), fem dage om ugen (five days a week).

forms.da: Jeg arbejder fem dage om ugen.
forms.en: I work five days a week.

sentence.da: Jeg træner tre gange **om ugen**.
sentence.en: I work out three times a week.

om året.explanation: "Om året" means "per year" and tells how often something happens. The same pattern works for a week: to gange om ugen (twice a week).

forms.da: Vi ses fire gange om året
forms.en: We see each other four times a year

sentence.da: Jeg besøger min mor to gange **om året**.
sentence.en: I visit my mother twice a year.

ombord.explanation: "Ombord" means "on board" a ship, plane or train: Hun går ombord på færgen (She goes on board the ferry). The opposite is i land (ashore): Vi går i land (We go ashore).

sentence.da: Alle er nu **ombord**, og færgen sejler.
sentence.en: Everyone is now on board and the ferry sails.

omfattende.explanation: "Omfattende" means "extensive", covering a lot of ground and having many parts. It is used for things such as plans, damage and changes, not for physical size: for a big house, use stor (big).

sentence.da: Rapporten er **omfattende** og har over to hundrede sider.
sentence.en: The report is extensive and has over two hundred pages.

omgivet.explanation: "Omgivet" means "surrounded", with something on every side. What is on the sides comes after af (by).

forms.en: The town is surrounded by forest

forms.da: Huset er omgivet af en mur
forms.en: The house is surrounded by a wall

sentence.da: Øen er **omgivet** af hav på alle sider.
sentence.en: The island is surrounded by sea on all sides.

omgående.explanation: "Omgående" means "immediately": with no delay at all. It is common in business letters, rules and warnings, and it is stricter than snart (soon).

sentence.da: Hvis dit kort bliver væk, skal du spærre det **omgående**.
sentence.en: If your card goes missing, you must block it immediately.

omhyggelig.explanation: "Omhyggelig" means "careful" or "meticulous", paying attention to every small detail so nothing goes wrong. It is about how you do work, while forsigtig (cautious) is about avoiding danger or damage: Vær forsigtig! (Be careful!)

sentence.da: Revisoren er **omhyggelig** og tjekker alle tal to gange.
sentence.en: The accountant is meticulous and checks every number twice.

omkring.explanation: "Omkring" means "around", both for a place and for a rough number or time: omkring tyve mennesker (about twenty people).

sentence.da: Der er mange træer **omkring** huset.
sentence.en: There are many trees around the house.

omsider.explanation: "Omsider" means "at last", used when something happens after a long wait. It adds a feeling of relief that the wait is over.

sentence.da: Efter tre timer kom toget **omsider**.
sentence.en: After three hours the train came at last.

omsorg.explanation: "En omsorg" means "care" in the sense of warm concern for a person who needs help, such as a parent for a child. It is about feelings and attention, not about objects.

sentence.da: Børn har brug for **omsorg** fra deres forældre.
sentence.en: Children need care from their parents.

omsorgsfuld.explanation: "Omsorgsfuld" means "caring", showing warm concern for someone who needs help. It is omsorg (care) plus -fuld (full of), the same ending as in smertefuld (painful).

sentence.da: Hun er **omsorgsfuld** og passer altid på sine venner.
sentence.en: She is caring and always looks after her friends.
