omstændelig.explanation: "Omstændelig" means "long-winded" or "elaborate": it takes more steps, words or time than needed. Do not mix it up with kompliceret (complicated), which is hard to understand. Something omstændelig may be easy, but it is long and fussy.

sentence.da: Ansøgningen er **omstændelig**, fordi man skal udfylde ti forskellige skemaer.
sentence.en: The application is elaborate, because you have to fill in ten different forms.

omtrent.explanation: "Omtrent" means "about", used with numbers, times and amounts. It also means "more or less": Det er omtrent færdigt (It is more or less done).

sentence.da: Turen til Aarhus tager **omtrent** to timer med bilen.
sentence.en: The trip to Aarhus takes about two hours by car.

omvendt.explanation: "Omvendt" means "the other way around", for something turned or reversed. At the start of a sentence it means "conversely" and introduces a contrast: Han er høj. Omvendt er hun lille (He is tall. Conversely, she is short).

sentence.da: Du har sat trøjen på **omvendt**, så mærket sidder foran.
sentence.en: You put the sweater on backwards, so the label is in front.

ond.explanation: "Ond" means "evil" or "wicked". It also means "painful" in set phrases: Det gør ondt (It hurts) and Jeg har ondt i hovedet (I have a headache).

sentence.da: Heksen i historien er meget **ond**.
sentence.en: The witch in the story is very evil.

ondskab.explanation: "En ondskab" means "evil" or "malice": the wish to hurt others on purpose. It is built from ond (bad) and -skab, as in venskab (friendship), so it is the state of being bad.

sentence.da: Han gjorde det af **ondskab** og ville såre hende.
sentence.en: He did it out of malice and wanted to hurt her.

ondt.explanation: "Ondt" means "pain" or "hurt". Danish says Jeg har ondt i maven, literally I have pain in the stomach, where English says my stomach hurts. Do not say Jeg er ondt (I am pain).

sentence.da: Jeg har **ondt** i maven.
sentence.en: My stomach hurts.

online.explanation: "Online" means "online", connected to the internet. It is spelled the same as in English and never changes: en online butik (an online store), et online kursus (an online course).

sentence.da: Man kan købe bøger **online**.
sentence.en: You can buy books online.

onsdag.explanation: "Onsdag" means "Wednesday". Like all day names, it starts with a small letter. Use på onsdag (on Wednesday, coming up) for the next one, and om onsdagen (on Wednesdays) for every week.

sentence.da: Efter tirsdag kommer **onsdag**.
sentence.en: After Tuesday comes Wednesday.

op.explanation: "Op" means "up", for moving up. Compare Kom op! (Come up!) with Han er oppe på loftet (He is up in the attic): oppe is for being there. It is also part of at stå op (to get up out of bed).

sentence.da: Katten hopper **op** på bordet.
sentence.en: The cat jumps up onto the table.

opad.explanation: "Opad" means "upward" and tells which way something moves. Words ending in -ad show direction, like udad (outward).

sentence.da: Røgen fra bålet stiger **opad** mod himlen.
sentence.en: The smoke from the fire rises upward toward the sky.

opbakning.explanation: "En opbakning" means "support" or "backing", when people stand behind a person, a plan or a decision. It is not physical support. Use til for what is backed: opbakning til forslaget (support for the proposal).

sentence.da: Planen fik stor **opbakning**, fordi næsten alle stemte for.
sentence.en: The plan got a lot of support because almost everyone voted for it.

opdateret.explanation: "Opdateret" means "updated", with the newest information or version. It also fits a person who knows the latest: Er du opdateret på nyhederne? (Are you up to date on the news?)

sentence.da: Min telefon er **opdateret** og virker nu fint.
sentence.en: My phone is updated and now works fine.

opdraget.explanation: "Opdraget" means "brought up", about the way someone was taught to behave. With godt (well) it means polite and well-behaved, and with dårligt (badly) it means rude. It is also used for pets.

sentence.da: Vores børn er **opdraget** til at sige tak og undskyld.
sentence.en: Our children are brought up to say thanks and sorry.

opfindsom.explanation: "Opfindsom" means "inventive": good at finding clever new ways to solve a problem, often with simple things you already have.

sentence.da: Hun er **opfindsom** og laver legetøj af gamle kasser.
sentence.en: She is inventive and makes toys out of old boxes.

opførsel.explanation: "Opførsel" means "behavior", how a person acts around others. Pæn opførsel means "good manners".

sentence.da: Hans **opførsel** over for børnene var meget pæn.
sentence.en: His behavior toward the children was very nice.

ophidset.explanation: "Ophidset" means "agitated" or "excited", very worked up and tense, as in en ophidset debat (a heated debate). It can also mean sexually aroused, so it is not the word for happy excitement.

sentence.da: Hun blev **ophidset** og råbte højt til dommeren.
sentence.en: She got worked up and shouted loudly at the referee.

opkast.explanation: "Et opkast" means "vomit", the matter itself. The act is at kaste op (to throw up), and opkast is built from the same two parts.

sentence.da: Efter maden fik hun kvalme og senere **opkast**.
sentence.en: After the meal she got nausea and later vomit.

opladning.explanation: "Opladning" means "charging", filling a battery up again. The action is at oplade (to charge).

sentence.da: Min telefon er på **opladning** lige nu.
sentence.en: My phone is charging right now.

oplagt.explanation: "Oplagt" means "obvious" for a choice or an answer that anyone can see. About a person, it means "in good form", full of energy and ready for the day: Hun er godt oplagt i dag (She is in good form today).

sentence.da: Det er en **oplagt** idé, fordi det er billigt og tæt på.
sentence.en: It is an obvious idea, because it is cheap and close by.

opmærksom.explanation: "Opmærksom" means "attentive" or "aware". With på (on) it means aware of something: Jeg er opmærksom på problemet (I am aware of the problem).

sentence.da: Min datter er **opmærksom** og lytter godt.
sentence.en: My daughter is attentive and listens well.

opmærksom på.explanation: "Opmærksom på" means "aware of" or "paying attention to". With at gøre nogen opmærksom på (to point something out to someone), you bring it to their attention: Jeg gjorde ham opmærksom på fejlen (I pointed out the mistake to him).

forms.da: Hun var ikke opmærksom på tiden
forms.en: She was not aware of the time

sentence.da: Du skal være **opmærksom på** cyklister, når du drejer.
sentence.en: You must pay attention to cyclists when you turn.

opmærksomhed.explanation: "Opmærksomhed" means "attention", the focus you give to someone or something. To pay attention, say at være opmærksom (to be attentive).

sentence.da: Babyen græder for at få **opmærksomhed**.
sentence.en: The baby cries to get attention.

oppe.explanation: "Oppe" means "up there", for where something is. Compare Katten hopper op på bordet (The cat jumps up onto the table) with Katten er oppe på bordet (The cat is up on the table). Er du oppe? (Are you up?) asks whether someone is out of bed.

sentence.da: Bogen ligger **oppe** på hylden.
sentence.en: The book is up on the shelf.

oprevet.explanation: "Oprevet" means "upset", emotionally thrown off after something unpleasant such as bad news or an argument. It is a churned-up feeling, stronger than just being sad.

sentence.da: Hun var **oprevet** efter skænderiet med sin bror.
sentence.en: She was upset after the quarrel with her brother.

oprigtig.explanation: "Oprigtig" means "sincere", meaning what you say and feel without pretending. It is about real feelings, while ærlig (honest) is more about telling the truth.

sentence.da: Hendes tak var **oprigtig**, og alle kunne mærke det.
sentence.en: Her thanks were sincere, and everyone could feel it.

oprindelig.explanation: "Oprindelig" means "original" in the sense of how it was at the start, before anything was changed. For something new and creative, Danes say original (original) instead.

sentence.da: Den gamle bro er stadig **oprindelig**, og ingen har ændret den.
sentence.en: The old bridge is still original, and no one has changed it.

oprørsk.explanation: "Oprørsk" means "rebellious": refusing to obey rules or people in charge. It is often used about children and teenagers, but also about a crowd that turns against those in power.

sentence.da: Teenageren blev **oprørsk** og ville ikke følge reglerne derhjemme.
sentence.en: The teenager became rebellious and would not follow the rules at home.

oprørt.explanation: "Oprørt" means "upset" or "stirred up", about feelings and also about water: et oprørt hav (a rough sea). For the cause, use over: oprørt over nyheden (upset about the news).

sentence.da: Hun blev **oprørt** over, at ingen havde ringet til hende.
sentence.en: She got upset that no one had called her.

opsyn.explanation: "Et opsyn" means "supervision": someone keeping an eye on people, animals or things so that nothing goes wrong. You mostly meet it in set phrases. Tilsyn (inspection) is a close word, often used for official checks.

sentence.da: Børn under ti år må ikke bade uden **opsyn**.
sentence.en: Children under ten must not swim without supervision.

optaget.explanation: "Optaget" means "busy", "taken" or "occupied". Use it for a phone line, a toilet or a seat that is in use. For a person it means no time right now: Jeg er optaget lige nu (I am busy right now).

sentence.da: Toilettet er **optaget** lige nu.
sentence.en: The toilet is occupied right now.

optimistisk.explanation: "Optimistisk" means "optimistic" and describes someone who expects things to go well. The opposite is pessimistisk (pessimistic).

sentence.da: Hun er **optimistisk** og tror altid på det bedste.
sentence.en: She is optimistic and always believes in the best.

opvaskemiddel.explanation: "Opvaskemiddel" means "dish soap". It is not for clothes; for those you use vaskepulver (laundry detergent).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **opvaskemiddel**, når jeg vasker op.
sentence.en: I use dish soap when I wash dishes.

orange.explanation: "Orange" means "orange", the color. For the fruit, Danes say en appelsin (an orange), not orange. The color word never changes, whatever it describes.

sentence.da: Gulerødder er **orange**.
sentence.en: Carrots are orange.

ordblind.explanation: "Ordblind" means "dyslexic", having a lasting difficulty with reading and spelling, which has nothing to do with intelligence. It is built from ord (word) and blind (blind), so "word-blind".

sentence.da: Hun er **ordblind** og har svært ved at stave.
sentence.en: She is dyslexic and finds it hard to spell.

ordentlig.explanation: "Ordentlig" means "proper" or "decent", done well and as it should be. For a person it means well-behaved: en ordentlig mand (a respectable man).

sentence.da: Du skal have **ordentlig** mad, ikke bare chips.
sentence.en: You must have proper food, not just chips.

organiseret.explanation: "Organiseret" means "organized", with everything in order and in its place. Add vel (well) in front for velorganiseret (well organized).

sentence.da: Hun er **organiseret** og kommer aldrig for sent.
sentence.en: She is organized and never comes late.

original.explanation: "Original" means "original": the first real one, not a copy. It can also mean "creative and new": en original idé (an original idea).

sentence.da: Det er en **original** tegning, ikke en kopi.
sentence.en: It is an original drawing, not a copy.

os.explanation: "Os" means "us". Compare Vi ser ham (We see him) with Han ser os (He sees us): vi is we, os is us.

related.en: you (more than one, after words like "med")

sentence.da: Vil du komme med **os**?
sentence.en: Do you want to come with us?

ost.explanation: "Ost" means "cheese". When you mean one kind of cheese, say en ost: en fransk ost means "a French cheese". Without en it is cheese in general.

sentence.da: **Ost** er lavet af mælk.
sentence.en: Cheese is made from milk.

otte.explanation: "Otte" means "eight". Do not mix it up with atten (eighteen): otte børn (eight children) but atten børn (eighteen children).

sentence.da: Efter syv kommer **otte**.
sentence.en: After seven comes eight.

ottende.explanation: "Ottende" means "eighth": den ottende dag (the eighth day). It is also used for dates: den ottende marts (the eighth of March).

sentence.da: Efter den syvende dag kommer den **ottende** dag.
sentence.en: After the seventh day comes the eighth day.

ovenover.explanation: "Ovenover" means "above", directly overhead or on the floor higher up in the same building. The opposite is nedenunder (below).

forms.en: It is on the shelf above

sentence.da: Vi hører skridt fra lejligheden **ovenover**, når naboen går rundt.
sentence.en: We hear steps from the apartment above when the neighbor walks around.

ovenpå.explanation: "Ovenpå" means "upstairs", on the floor above you. It works for where something is and for going there: Jeg bor ovenpå (I live upstairs), Jeg går ovenpå (I go upstairs). The opposite is nedenunder (downstairs).

sentence.da: Soveværelset er **ovenpå**, og køkkenet er nede.
sentence.en: The bedroom is upstairs, and the kitchen is down.

over.explanation: "Over" means "over", above or "across". Compare Lampen hænger over bordet (The lamp hangs above the table) with Han går over gaden (He walks across the street). With amounts it means "more than": over to timer (more than two hours).

sentence.da: Lampen hænger **over** bordet.
sentence.en: The lamp hangs over the table.

overalt.explanation: "Overalt" means "everywhere", in every place. It can also start a sentence for emphasis: Overalt er der blomster (Everywhere there are flowers). The opposite is ingen steder (nowhere).

sentence.da: Jeg leder **overalt** efter nøglen.
sentence.en: I look everywhere for the key.

overarbejde.explanation: "Overarbejde" means "overtime", the work done beyond your normal hours. Danes say at arbejde over (to work overtime) for doing it.

sentence.da: Når jeg arbejder ud over min normale tid, er det **overarbejde**.
sentence.en: When I work beyond my normal time, it is overtime.

overbevisende.explanation: "Overbevisende" means "convincing", good at making people believe or accept something. It comes from at overbevise (to convince), the same way "convincing" comes from "convince".

sentence.da: Forklaringen var **overbevisende**, og alle troede på hende.
sentence.en: The explanation was convincing, and everyone believed her.

overdreven.explanation: "Overdreven" means "exaggerated" or "excessive", more than is reasonable or true. It can describe an amount or a way of telling something: overdreven høflighed (excessive politeness).

sentence.da: Reaktionen var **overdreven**, fordi fejlen kun var lille.
sentence.en: The reaction was exaggerated because the mistake was only small.

overfladisk.explanation: "Overfladisk" means "superficial", touching only the outside of something. It fits knowledge and people: overfladisk viden (superficial knowledge).

sentence.da: Vi kender kun hinanden **overfladisk**, men vi hilser altid.
sentence.en: We only know each other superficially, but we always say hello.

overfor.explanation: "Overfor" means "opposite" or "across from": Banken ligger overfor skolen (The bank is across from the school). It can also mean "facing": Jeg står overfor et valg (I am facing a choice).

sentence.da: Min ven bor **overfor** biblioteket.
sentence.en: My friend lives across from the library.

overfyldt.explanation: "Overfyldt" means "overcrowded" or "overfull", with more in it than there is room for. It also fits things, not just places with people: en overfyldt skuffe (a stuffed drawer).

sentence.da: Bussen var **overfyldt**, og mange måtte stå op hele vejen.
sentence.en: The bus was overcrowded, and many had to stand all the way.

overhovedet.explanation: "Overhovedet" means "at all" and is used with ikke (not) or in questions: Jeg forstår overhovedet ikke (I do not understand at all).

forms.en: It is not difficult at all.

sentence.da: Jeg har **overhovedet** ikke tid i dag.
sentence.en: I have no time at all today.

overlegen.explanation: "Overlegen" means "superior": clearly better or stronger than others. About a person's manner, it means looking down on others: Han talte med en overlegen tone (He spoke in a superior tone).

sentence.da: Holdet var **overlegen** og vandt kampen med lethed.
sentence.en: The team was superior and won the match with ease.

overlevelse.explanation: "En overlevelse" means "survival", staying alive despite danger or hardship. The action is at overleve (to survive), and overlevelse is the same idea as a thing.

sentence.da: Uden vand og mad er der ingen **overlevelse** i ørkenen.
sentence.en: Without water and food there is no survival in the desert.

overmodig.explanation: "Overmodig" means "overconfident": so sure of yourself that you take risks or ignore danger. It is built from over (too much) and mod (courage), so it is courage that has gone too far.

sentence.da: Han var **overmodig** og gik ud på den tynde is.
sentence.en: He was overconfident and went out onto the thin ice.

overordnet.explanation: "Overordnet" means "overall" and "superior". As "overall" it looks at the big picture: overordnet set (broadly speaking). As "superior" it means higher in rank, and en overordnet (a superior) is a person above you at work.

sentence.da: Min **overordnet** på arbejdet fordeler opgaverne til os andre.
sentence.en: My superior at work hands out the tasks to the rest of us.

overraskende.explanation: "Overraskende" means "surprising" and describes news or events that you did not expect. To say how you feel, use overrasket: Jeg er overrasket (I am surprised).

sentence.da: Resultatet var **overraskende**.
sentence.en: The result was surprising.

overskuelig.explanation: "Overskuelig" means "manageable" or "clear": easy to see as a whole, because it is small or well organized. It fits a plan, a budget, a text or a situation. The opposite is uoverskuelig (hard to survey).

sentence.da: En **overskuelig** plan med få trin er lettere at følge.
sentence.en: A clear plan with few steps is easier to follow.

overskyet.explanation: "Overskyet" means "overcast", with the whole sky covered by clouds. It is stronger than skyet (cloudy), which can mean just a few clouds.

sentence.da: Himlen er **overskyet** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is overcast today.

overvågning.explanation: "En overvågning" means "surveillance", careful watching of people, places or systems, often by cameras. It is also used for watching a patient in a hospital: overvågning af patienten (watching over the patient).

sentence.da: Kameraerne i butikken er en slags **overvågning**.
sentence.en: The cameras in the store are a kind of surveillance.

overvægt.explanation: "En overvægt" means "overweight", carrying more body weight than is healthy. Danes say at have overvægt (to be overweight). At the airport it also means baggage over the weight limit.

sentence.da: **Overvægt** kan give problemer med hjertet og leddene.
sentence.en: Overweight can cause problems with the heart and joints.

overvældende.explanation: "Overvældende" means "overwhelming", so big or intense that it is hard to take in, for good things and bad: en overvældende opgave (an overwhelming task). It describes the cause, while overvældet (overwhelmed) describes how you feel.

sentence.da: Udsigten fra toppen var **overvældende**, og vi blev stille.
sentence.en: The view from the top was overwhelming, and we went quiet.

overvældet.explanation: "Overvældet" means "overwhelmed", the feeling of being hit by something too big or too much, in a good way or a bad way. It describes how you feel, while overvældende (overwhelming) describes the thing that causes it.

sentence.da: Hun var helt **overvældet** af alle gaverne og kortene.
sentence.en: She was completely overwhelmed by all the gifts and cards.
